definition: Commendation means a formal, official statement or act of praise, such as an award.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word commendation. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know commendation should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The museum's trustees voted unanimously to issue a written commendation to the conservator who saved the fire-damaged murals.
A compliment is casual, everyday praise; a commendation is official praise made formally and on the record.
A medal goes one step past a commendation — the official praise becomes a physical decoration pinned on for all to see.

A citation is a formal written mention that can serve many purposes -- honoring a soldier, penalizing a driver, or crediting a source. A commendation is narrower: it is official praise and nothing else. Every commendation honors; a citation might just as easily fine you or footnote you.

A tribute is a public act or expression of honor -- a speech, a dedicated song, a moment of silence -- and anyone who wants to show respect can offer one. A commendation comes from an authority: official praise issued formally and entered on the record. A fan can pay tribute; only the board issues a commendation.

Commendation means a formal, official statement or act of praise, such as an award.

When the ransomware attack froze the hospital's systems, night-shift pharmacist Ellis Okafor hand-checked every medication order against paper records for eighteen straight hours, and not one dose went out wrong.

Two months later, the hospital board did something it had done only four times in its history: it entered a formal commendation into the official record, praising Okafor by name and describing exactly what his diligence had prevented.
The board's formal, on-the-record statement of praise — voted on, written down, and entered into the official record — is what makes this a commendation rather than a simple thank-you.
formal, institutional; an act or document, not a feeling

A commendation is a specific, official act of praise — a certificate, resolution, or statement read into the record — which keeps it in a different lane from renown (general earned fame), adulation (gushing unofficial admiration), and idolatrous devotion (worship that has gone too far); it names paperwork and ceremony, never an emotion.

In March, an envelope bearing the parks department seal arrived at the ranger station, addressed to Ruiz.
Inside was a single page on official letterhead: a commendation for her work during the October fire, when she cleared forty campsites in under two hours.
The letter was short, but it was signed by the director, and a copy now sits in her permanent service file.
Her coworkers had already praised her back in October, and hikers still thanked her on the trail.
The letter was different, Ruiz thought — kind words fade, but official praise on the record follows you.
